subject: Cross-cloud listing governance: SKU split and regional prioritization
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Team <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>, Azure Co-sell <azure-cosell@microsoft.com>, GCP Partner <marketplace@gcp-partner.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-cloud listing governance: SKU split and regional prioritization

Team / partners —

We need a sharp decision this week on how we will structure marketplace listings across AWS, Azure, and GCP for the upcoming Q3 push. The ask is narrow: agree the SKU names/tiers we will list per cloud, the initial regional rollout, and the co-sell eligibility criteria so Partnerships can begin enrollment.

High-level constraints:
- Minimal engineering lift for first listing (prefer 2–3 SKUs per cloud).
- Azure requires a commercial marketplace submission + co-sell enrollment to be visible to their GTM teams.
- AWS prefers SaaS subscription or metered product SKU depending on deployment model.
- GCP marketplace has regional constraints for EU data residency that may force separate SKUs.

Proposal (please comment inline):
- SKUs: Entry, Standard, Enterprise (use same names across clouds if possible).
- Regions phase 1: US (us-east/us-west) + EU (eu-west), APAC later.
- Co-sell triggers: 3 closed pilot deals OR $30k ARR (whichever first) + SOC 2 evidence and SSO integration.

Ben / Karthik — can you attach the SKU mapping and call out any gating tech work? Soojin / Jonas — Partnerships, flag anything from the marketplace programs or co-sell playbooks that would block an expedited listing.

Attachments: sku_mapping_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Marketplace GTM | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud listing governance: SKU split and regional prioritization

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 09:12, Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Proposal (please comment inline):
> - SKUs: Entry, Standard, Enterprise (use same names across clouds if possible).
> - Regions phase 1: US (us-east/us-west) + EU (eu-west), APAC later.
> - Co-sell triggers: 3 closed pilot deals OR $30k ARR + SOC 2 and SSO.

Agree with Naomi's framing. I've attached a mapping (sku_mapping_v2.xlsx) with the recommended resource/usage model and the minimum engineering changes for each cloud. Summary below:

- AWS: support 3 SKUs. Prefer SaaS subscription SKUs for Dedicated customers and metered SaaS for usage-based Starter tier. Estimated listing work: 2 sprints (billing + SaaS contract + listing metadata). Co-sell note: AWS asks that we also enable consolidated billing for marketplace-managed entitlements (we can do this, needs billing lead).

- Azure: recommend 2 SKUs (Standard, Enterprise). Azure's commercial marketplace has stricter certification for metered billing; limiting to two SKUs reduces re-cert cycles. Co-sell enrollment requires MAPP (Marketplace Accelerate) doc and a technical integration checklist; timeline ~4 weeks once docs ready.

- GCP: 2 SKUs but split by region for EU compliance (Standard-EU, Enterprise-EU). GCP's marketplace supports regional listing metadata; engineering needs a small switch for data residency flag.

Risks / asks:
- If we insist on identical SKU names everywhere, spec differences may confuse customers (metered vs subscription). Recommend consistent tier names but cloud-specific usage notes in listing text.
- Need SOC 2 report and SSO/SCIM work to meet co-sell gating.

Attachments: sku_mapping_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), product_listing_notes.md

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Product Manager, GTM | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
From: AWS Marketplace Team <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud listing governance: SKU split and regional prioritization

Thanks Naomi —

We reviewed the initial SKU mapping and the attached spreadsheet. A couple quick clarifications for AWS Marketplace:

1) Co-sell eligibility: AWS typically requires a published SaaS contract + listed pricing. For co-sell with APN, the payment model (SaaS subscription vs metered) can affect which GTM programs you’re eligible for. If you want APN co-sell fast, subscription SKUs are easier to enroll.

2) Entitlements: For metered SKUs we need a usage-reporting endpoint and metering dimensions documented during listing.

3) Regional notes: AWS does not require separate SKUs per region by default, but if you enforce data residency per customer you should reflect that in the listing and offer a dedicated EU SKU.

We can start a listing intake once you confirm: (A) final SKU names and billing types per SKU, (B) contact for billing integration, and (C) desired go-live region(s). I've attached our co-sell checklist.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Team
aws-marketplace@amazon.com
Attachments: cloud_co-sell_checklist_AWS.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud listing governance: SKU split and regional prioritization

Internal summary and decision (approving to proceed):

After reviewing Ben's mapping and AWS feedback, agreed next steps:
- SKU model: Use consistent tier names across clouds: Entry / Standard / Enterprise.
  - AWS: Entry (metered SaaS), Standard (subscription), Enterprise (subscription + dedicated contract).
  - Azure: Standard, Enterprise (limit to 2 SKUs for certification speed). Entry will be a channel offer (link to offer) but not in initial commercial listing.
  - GCP: Standard-EU, Enterprise-EU for initial launch (EU residency flagged).

- Regions for initial rollout: US + EU. APAC targeted for Q4 pending localized pricing and partner approvals.

- Co-sell gating: require SOC 2 in doc folder, SSO + SCIM integration complete, and a minimum of 3 pilot wins OR $30k ARR to request active co-sell outreach. Partnerships to start enrollment with AWS and Azure now; GCP enrollment in parallel but gating may be slower.

Owners & deadlines:
- Ben Carter: finalize SKU descriptions & pricing by 2027-03-18 (owner: ben@redwood.ai).
- Karthik Iyer: engineering scope and billing integration plan by 2027-03-25 (owner: karthik@redwood.ai).
- Soojin Lee: begin commercial paperwork and MAPP docs for Azure, start AWS APN intake by 2027-03-15 (owner: soojin@redwood.ai).

Naomi — if you agree with owners/timing, I'll send out the enrollment emails to AWS & Azure and schedule a standing 30-min sync next week.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
